name: libunwind
notes: extra_checkout_dirs (cmake/, runtimes/cmake/): libunwind/CMakeLists.txt is not self-contained -- it include()s shared LLVM CMake utility modules from these two sibling top-level directories (HandleCompilerRT.cmake and LLVMCheckCompilerLinkerFlag.cmake live in cmake/Modules/, HandleFlags.cmake lives in runtimes/cmake/Modules/), which a sparse-checkout of just libunwind/ alone does not carry. Confirmed for real: the first configure attempt without these failed with three separate "include could not find requested file" errors, one per missing module, only surfacing them one at a time as each earlier include() itself got past its own missing-file error. tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's fetch_recipe() copies these as siblings of libunwind/ under the shared source root, matching the relative ../cmake path libunwind/CMakeLists.txt itself expects.

macOS is deliberately excluded via target_os: Darwin's own libSystem provides a real system unwinder (compact unwind info, not the Itanium DWARF-CFI-based mechanism this project's other two hosts need), and the existing macOS crt-libcxx-smoke run already exercises real exception throw/catch successfully with no libunwind at all -- matches upstream LLVM's own default of LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER=OFF for Apple targets. Linux and Windows both build this from source rather than linking a host-installed libunwind package: a Linux distro's own libunwind-dev is easy to reach for, but linking it would put a DT_NEEDED on a library this project does not own or control the build of into every C++ binary this project ships (including its own libc++.so in the rootfs) -- a real runtime dependency, not a cosmetic shortcut, and one this project has consistently avoided elsewhere (../libcxx and ../libcxxabi are built from source rather than using host libstdc++/libc++ for the same reason; -lpthread/-lrt were absorbed into libc specifically so a host pthread/rt library could never leak into a Bionic-shaped binary; CRTGFX_ENABLE_SKIA's own policy states outright "never link host libc++ as a substitute"). This is a genuinely different case from CI's libc++-dev/libc++abi-dev install (see HISTORY.md's 2026-08-21 CI entry): that is a build-time-only requirement so Clang's own compiler-ABI-detection step can run while compiling *this project itself* -- it never ends up linked into anything this project ships.

Android removed the old platform/external/libunwind project in 2021; the current source policy is AOSP toolchain/llvm-project/libunwind (a full LLVM monorepo mirror -- fetched via a partial clone + cone sparse-checkout scoped to just the libunwind/ subpath, not the whole tree, confirmed to keep the fetch to tens of MB rather than the full monorepo).

libcxxabi's own recipe.json does NOT reference this recipe's source/build at all (no LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER/LIBCXXABI_LIBUNWIND_INCLUDES wiring): the plain, default Itanium ABI surface libcxxabi already compiles against (_Unwind_RaiseException/_Unwind_Resume/etc.) is exactly what a real libunwind -- LLVM's own, whether host-provided on Linux or built here on Windows -- already exports, so the only real cross-reference needed is a link-time one, added in tools/crt-c++ (Windows: the sysroot-staged archive/import library this recipe produces; Linux: a bare -lunwind against the host install). No LIBCXXABI-side CMake change needed on either host.
